sections.title: The letter elle
paragraphs: The letter is called (elle) /ɛl/. Its main sound is heard in (lune) /lyn/, which means moon. This letter makes one spoken sound, but in some words it stays silent.

sections.title: Pronouncing the letter
paragraphs: Put the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Let the air flow smoothly around the sides of your tongue. Turn your voice on so your throat vibrates.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: In most positions, you pronounce this letter as heard in (bal) /bal/. At the end of a few specific words, the letter is not pronounced, such as in (fusil) /fy.zi/ and (outil) /u.ti/.

sections.title: Common learner mistakes
paragraphs: At the end of a syllable, keep the back of your tongue flat and low. Do not pull the back of your tongue up like in the English word ball. Keep the tip firmly forward against the ridge behind your upper teeth.
